q.s: The first Harappan seal, bearing a unicorn, was reported by Alexander Cunningham from:
q.x: Cunningham reported the first (unicorn) seal from Harappa in 1872-75.

q.s: A Persian Gulf-type button seal, evidence of Harappan overseas trade, was found at:
q.x: The Persian Gulf-type button seal comes from the port-town of Lothal in Gujarat.

q.s: Which of the following has NOT been found in any Harappan city?
q.x: No temple (nor royal palace) has been found in Harappan cities; worship was probably domestic or open-air.

q.s: Heavily jewelled female terracotta figurines found at Harappa are generally identified as the:
q.x: The jewelled female figurines are taken to represent the Mother Goddess; terracottas were crude objects of common people.

q.s: Which of the following Harappan sites is NOT in Gujarat?
q.x: Chanhudaro, known for its bead-making and toy carts, is in Sindh; the other three are in Gujarat.

q.s: The Battle of Ten Kings (Dasarajna) mentioned in the Rig Veda was won by:
q.x: Sudas, the Bharata king, defeated a confederacy of ten tribes on the Parushni (Ravi).

q.s: After the Battle of Ten Kings, the Bharatas and the Purus united to form the:
q.x: The Bharatas and the defeated Purus merged to form the Kurus.

q.s: In the Later Vedic period, large Shrauta sacrifices such as the Rajasuya chiefly strengthened the position of the:
q.x: These rites needed many priests and huge dakshina, which raised the power of the Brahmanas.

q.s: In the ancient forms of Hindu marriage, marriage by purchase was known as:
q.x: Asura marriage was by purchase; Rakshasa marriage was by capture.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the eight forms of Hindu marriage?
q.x: The eight forms are Brahma, Daiva, Arsha, Prajapatya, Asura, Gandharva, Rakshasa and Paishacha; Rakshasa was marriage by capture.

q.s: Among the Pancha Mahayajnas, the Brahma-yajna was meant for:
q.x: Brahma-yajna = Vedic study; Deva = gods; Pitri = ancestors; Nri/Atithi = guests.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the Pancha Mahayajnas?
q.x: The five are Brahma, Deva, Pitri, Bhuta and Nri (Atithi) yajnas; the Ashvamedha was a royal sacrifice.

q.s: In early historic India the term 'Setthi' (Shreshthi) referred to a:
q.x: Setthi was a rich merchant-banker; a kusidin was a usurer.

q.s: The term 'Gahapati' in early Buddhist texts denoted a:
q.x: Gahapati was a wealthy householder or landowner; the caravan leader was the sarthavaha.

q.s: The Hathigumpha inscription at Udayagiri near Bhubaneswar belongs to:
q.x: Hathigumpha is Kharavela's record; Junagadh is Rudradaman's.

q.s: The Nanaghat inscription is associated with the Satavahana queen:
q.x: Nanaghat belongs to Naganika; Gautami Balasri issued the Nasik inscription.

q.s: Which edict of Ashoka gave the rajukas judicial powers and a three-day respite to condemned prisoners?
q.x: Pillar Edict IV deals with the rajukas and the three-day respite; PE II defines Dhamma.

q.s: Ashoka's Schism edict is found at all of the following places EXCEPT:
q.x: The Schism edict is at Sarnath, Sanchi and Kaushambi; Kalsi has a set of Major Rock Edicts.

q.s: The astronomical work Khandakhadyaka was written by:
q.x: Khandakhadyaka is Brahmagupta's work; Aryabhata wrote the Aryabhatiya.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Bhaskara I used a circle for zero in 729 CE.
The 876 CE inscription showing zero as a circle is at Mandasor.
q.x: Bhaskara I's date is 629 CE and the 876 CE inscription is at Gwalior.

q.s: Which mathematician first laid down the arithmetic rules for operations with zero?
q.x: Brahmagupta formalised the rules for zero; Aryabhata used zero and place value.

q.s: The Chudamani Vihara at Nagapattinam was built by a Sailendra king with the permission of:
q.x: Sri Mara Vijayottungavarman built it with Rajaraja I's permission.

q.s: Which of the following temples was NOT built by the Imperial Cholas?
q.x: The Kailasanatha temple was built by the Pallava Rajasimha.

q.s: Vijayalaya, founder of the Imperial Chola line, captured Thanjavur around 850 CE from the:
q.x: Vijayalaya, a Pallava feudatory, took Thanjavur from the Muttaraiyars.

q.s: Which Chola ruler defeated the last Pallava king Aparajita and ended Pallava rule?
q.x: Aditya I defeated Aparajita and annexed the Pallava territory.

q.s: In Chola territorial administration, the unit immediately above the nadu was the:
q.x: The order was ur - nadu - kottam/valanadu - mandalam; kurram was another name for the nadu.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a territorial unit of Chola administration?
q.x: A ghatika was a centre of learning; ur, nadu, valanadu and mandalam were territorial units.

q.s: The historian Burton Stein described the Chola state as:
q.x: Stein's 'segmentary state' model challenged Nilakanta Sastri's view of a centralised Chola state.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a ruler of the Imperial Chola dynasty?
q.x: Krishna III was a Rashtrakuta king who defeated the Cholas at Takkolam.

q.s: Which Sultan forbade nobles to hold feasts or form marriage alliances without royal permission?
q.x: Alauddin's ordinance aimed at the gatherings and intermarriages that Barani saw as breeding revolt.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a measure of Alauddin Khalji?
o: Dagh and chehra for the army
q.x: The silver tanka was introduced by Iltutmish.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Ibrahim Lodi wrote under the pen name Gulrukhi.
Timur left Khizr Khan as governor of Lahore.
Khizr Khan founded the Sayyid dynasty in 1451.
q.x: Gulrukhi was Sikandar Lodi's pen name; Khizr Khan was governor of Multan and founded the Sayyid dynasty in 1414.

q.s: The Sayyid dynasty was founded in 1414 by:
q.x: Khizr Khan, left by Timur as governor of Multan, took Delhi in 1414.

q.s: In the Delhi Sultanate, 'Khams' was:
o: The state's one-fifth share of war booty
q.x: Khams was the state's one-fifth of booty and treasure-trove; jizya was the poll tax, kharaj the land tax, zakat the religious tax.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a tax of the Delhi Sultanate?
q.x: Chauth was a Maratha levy.

q.s: Humayun's Tomb in Delhi was built by:
q.x: Humayun's widow Bega Begum built the tomb.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a measure of Sher Shah Suri?
q.x: The mansabdari system was Akbar's; Sher Shah issued the rupiya and used patta and qabuliyat.

q.s: Akbar was born in 1542 at:
q.x: Akbar was born at Amarkot in Sind while Humayun was in flight.

q.s: Humayun was decisively defeated by Sher Shah in 1540 at the Battle of:
q.x: Kannauj (Bilgram), 1540, drove Humayun out of India; Chausa was 1539.

q.s: The Second Battle of Panipat (1556) was fought between Akbar's forces and:
q.x: Bairam Khan, for Akbar, defeated Hemu in 1556.

q.s: Which of the following battles was NOT fought by Humayun?
q.x: Panipat II (1556) was fought after Humayun's death, by Akbar's forces against Hemu.

q.s: Under Akbar, the Mir Bakhshi was in charge of:
q.x: The Mir Bakhshi handled military matters - dagh, chehra and promotions.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a central minister under Akbar?
q.x: The faujdar was a district (sarkar) officer; the Mir Saman managed the royal household and karkhanas.

q.s: The Jat revolt of 1669 in the Mathura (Tilpat) region was led by:
q.x: Gokula led the 1669 revolt; Rajaram later plundered Akbar's tomb; Churaman built the Bharatpur power.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a revolt against Aurangzeb?
q.x: The Moplah rebellion took place in Malabar in 1921.

q.s: In Mughal administration the Muhtasib was responsible for:
q.x: The Muhtasib enforced public morals; the Bakhshi handled military pay.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT an officer of Mughal provincial or local administration?
q.x: The Peshwa was a Maratha minister.

q.s: What was an important economic consequence of collecting land revenue in cash under the Mughal zabt system?
o: It monetised the rural economy and linked peasants to markets
q.x: Cash demand forced peasants to sell produce, monetising the rural economy.

q.s: The Dars-e-Nizami curriculum of Islamic education was founded by:
q.x: Mulla Nizamuddin of Firangi Mahal, Sihali, framed the Dars-e-Nizami.

q.s: Which European traveller observed that Mughal India had no middle class, only the very rich and the very poor?
q.x: Francois Bernier made this observation.

q.s: With which region is the Bhakti saint Chaitanya associated?
q.x: Chaitanya worked in Bengal (and Orissa); Mirabai belonged to Rajasthan.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of Bhakti saint and region is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Mirabai belonged to Rajasthan.

q.s: Which of the following Maharashtra saints was a contemporary of Shivaji?
q.x: Tukaram (17th century) was Shivaji's contemporary; Namdev lived in the Tughlaq age.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Namdev lived long before Shivaji, in the Tughlaq age.
Tukaram lived in the Tughlaq age.
Janabai was a disciple of Tukaram.
Namdev was a contemporary of Shivaji.
q.x: Namdev (1270-1350) was much earlier; Tukaram was Shivaji's contemporary; Janabai was Namdev's disciple.

q.s: Alberuni compared Sufi ideas with Patanjali's Yoga Sutra and the Gita in his work:
q.x: Alberuni's Kitab-ul-Hind (Tahqiq-i-Hind) contains the comparison.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a Sufi silsila?
q.x: The Naths were a yogic sect, not a Sufi order.

q.s: Shivaji signed the Treaty of Purandar (1665) with:
q.x: By Purandar, signed with Jai Singh, Shivaji ceded 23 of his 35 forts.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Rajaram was sent into Mughal service under the Treaty of Purandar.
By the Treaty of Purandar Shivaji ceded all his forts.
Sambhaji was sent into Mughal service under the Treaty of Purandar.
Afzal Khan was a general of the Mughals.
q.x: Sambhaji went into Mughal service; Shivaji ceded 23 of 35 forts; Afzal Khan was a Bijapur general.

q.s: The Nizam conceded the Maratha claims to chauth and sardeshmukhi after the Battle of:
q.x: Baji Rao I defeated the Nizam at Palkhed in 1728.

q.s: Chauth, collected by the Marathas, was what share of the land revenue?
q.x: Chauth was one-fourth; sardeshmukhi an additional one-tenth.

q.s: Madras was founded in 1639 by Francis Day along with:
q.x: Francis Day and Andrew Cogan founded Madras with the help of the Damerla brothers.

q.s: India's first municipal corporation was set up in 1688 at:
q.x: Madras got the first municipal corporation in 1688.

q.s: The English settlement of Armagaon (1626) on the Andhra coast is identified with:
q.x: Armagaon, named after Armugam Mudali, is Dugarajapatnam in today's Tirupati district.

q.s: The English factory at Visakhapatnam was set up in:
q.x: The Visakhapatnam factory dates to 1682; Machilipatnam to 1611.

q.s: Who replaced Dupleix and signed the Treaty of Pondicherry (1754)?
q.x: Godeheu replaced Dupleix; the treaty left the Second Carnatic War inconclusive.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: The Treaty of Pondicherry ended the war with a decisive French victory.
The Treaty of Pondicherry (1754) left the Second Carnatic War inconclusive.
Dupleix himself signed the Treaty of Pondicherry.
q.x: Godeheu replaced Dupleix and signed the treaty, which was inconclusive.

q.s: The only Governor-General to have been impeached in the British Parliament was:
q.x: Hastings was impeached (trial 1788-95) and finally acquitted.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT among the charges against Warren Hastings?
o: Treatment of the Begums of Awadh
q.x: The Permanent Settlement (1793) was Cornwallis's measure.

q.s: The Supreme Court at Calcutta was established under the:
q.x: The Regulating Act provided the Supreme Court (set up 1774).

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a provision of the Regulating Act, 1773?
o: Subordination of Bombay and Madras to Bengal
q.x: The Board of Control came with Pitt's India Act, 1784.

q.s: Raja Rammohan Roy protested against which of the following measures?
q.x: Rammohan protested the 1823 Press Ordinance and the Jury Act of 1827.

q.s: Raja Rammohan Roy is associated with all of the following EXCEPT:
q.x: The Arya Samaj was founded by Dayananda Saraswati in 1875.

q.s: Who became the first non-Brahmin acharya of the Brahmo Samaj?
q.x: Debendranath made Keshab Chandra Sen acharya, the first non-Brahmin in that office.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: The Tattvabodhini Patrika was published in English.
Debendranath Tagore joined the Brahmo Samaj in 1859.
The Tattvabodhini Patrika was published in Bengali.
The Tattvabodhini Sabha merged into the Prarthana Samaj.
q.x: Debendranath joined the Brahmo Samaj in 1843; the Sabha merged into the Brahmo Samaj in 1859.

q.s: Who among the following was a founder of the Sadharan Brahmo Samaj (1878)?
q.x: Ananda Mohan Bose and Shivnath Shastri broke away after Keshab's Cooch Behar marriage.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT associated with the Brahmo Samaj?
q.x: Dayananda founded the Arya Samaj.

q.s: The movement for the use of spoken (vyavaharika) Telugu in literature and education was led by:
q.x: Gidugu Ramamurthy led the vyavaharika movement; the Vyavaharika Bhashodyama Samstha was formed in 1910.

q.s: Kandukuri Veeresalingam was born in 1848 at:
q.x: Veeresalingam was born at Rajahmundry, the centre of his reform work.

q.s: Kandukuri Veeresalingam is associated with all of the following EXCEPT:
q.x: Kanyasulkam is Gurajada Apparao's play.

q.s: Who was the first secretary of the All India Anti-Untouchability League (1932)?
q.x: Thakkar Bapa was the first secretary; G.D. Birla was its president.

q.s: The Independent Labour Party, which won 15 of 17 seats contested in 1937, was founded by:
q.x: Ambedkar founded the Independent Labour Party in 1936.

q.s: The Indian Association of Calcutta (1876) was founded by Surendranath Banerjea and:
q.x: The Indian Association, a pre-Congress body, was founded on 26 July 1876.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a pre-Congress political association?
q.x: Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society in 1905.

q.s: The Ghadar Party, founded in 1913 at San Francisco, is chiefly associated with:
q.x: Har Dayal led the Ghadar movement; the outbreak of the First World War triggered its 1915 revolt plan.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a leader of the Ghadar movement?
q.x: Shyamji Krishna Varma founded India House in London (1905).

q.s: The ship Komagata Maru (1914) began its voyage to Vancouver from:
q.x: The ship left Hong Kong on 4 April 1914 and called at Shanghai, Moji and Yokohama.

q.s: The Nehru Report (1928) demanded:
q.x: The Nehru Report sought dominion status and joint electorates with reservation.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a member of the Nehru Committee (1928)?
q.x: Jinnah rejected the report and later put forward his Fourteen Points.

q.s: Gandhi's 'Great Trial' at Ahmedabad (1922) arose from his articles in:
q.x: He was charged under Section 124A for articles in Young India and sentenced to six years.

q.s: Which of the following journals was NOT associated with Gandhi?
q.x: Kesari was Tilak's paper.

q.s: The Calcutta special session of the Congress (September 1920), which approved non-cooperation, was presided over by:
q.x: Lajpat Rai presided at Calcutta; Vijayaraghavachariar presided at Nagpur (December 1920).

q.s: Gandhi formally launched the Non-Cooperation Movement on 1 August 1920, the day of the death of:
q.x: Tilak died on 1 August 1920; Gandhi returned his Kaiser-i-Hind medal that day.

q.s: When the Swaraj Party was formed in January 1923 with C.R. Das as president, its secretary was:
q.x: Das and Motilal Nehru founded the Congress-Khilafat Swaraj Party; Patel, Prasad and Rajaji were No-changers.

q.s: C.R. Das's council-entry proposal was defeated at which Congress session of 1922?
q.x: Defeated at Gaya, Das resigned the presidency and formed the Swaraj Party.

q.s: Which region was drawn into the national movement during the Civil Disobedience Movement through the Khudai Khidmatgars?
q.x: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan's Khudai Khidmatgars brought the NWFP into the movement.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a part of the Civil Disobedience Movement?
q.x: Chauri Chaura (1922) ended the Non-Cooperation Movement.

q.s: The Poona Pact (1932) was signed by B.R. Ambedkar for the depressed classes and, for the caste Hindus, by:
q.x: Malaviya signed for the caste Hindus after Gandhi's fast at Yerwada.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: The Poona Pact retained separate electorates for the depressed classes.
The Poona Pact also reserved seats for the depressed classes in the Central Legislature.
The Poona Pact reserved seats only in the provincial legislatures.
The Poona Pact reduced the seats given by the Communal Award.
q.x: It replaced separate electorates with a joint electorate, raised provincial seats to 148 and reserved 18% of general Central seats.

q.s: The Simla Conference on the Wavell Plan was held in:
q.x: Wavell became Viceroy in October 1943; the Simla Conference was in June 1945.

q.s: Who presided over the Ramgarh session of the Congress (March 1940)?
q.x: Maulana Azad presided at Ramgarh.

q.s: The United Bengal plan of 1947 was put forward by Sarat Chandra Bose and:
q.x: The Bose-Suhrawardy plan was rejected by both the Congress and the League.

q.s: Who suggested an immediate transfer of power in 1947 on the basis of dominion status?
q.x: V.P. Menon's dominion-status proposal shaped the Mountbatten Plan.

q.s: Who was the Congress President when the AICC accepted partition in June 1947?
q.x: Kripalani presided; G.B. Pant moved and Azad seconded the resolution.

q.s: Gandhi described 'passive resistance', as distinct from satyagraha, as the:
q.x: Gandhi held that passive resistance was the weapon of the weak, satyagraha that of the strongest.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a principle of satyagraha as taught by Gandhi?
q.x: Satyagraha aims to change the opponent's heart, not to defeat him.

q.s: Gandhi's Gujarati paraphrase of Ruskin's 'Unto This Last' (1908) was titled:
q.x: Gandhi called his version 'Sarvodaya' - the welfare of all.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a part of Gandhian economic thought?
q.x: Gandhi favoured village industries and decentralisation.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Civil Disobedience Movement in Andhra is correct?
o: In the villages it included salt-making and cutting toddy palms.
It was confined to the towns and never reached the villages.
It did not involve picketing of foreign-cloth shops.
Volunteers of the Eluru National School kept away from it.
q.x: In towns it took the form of picketing foreign-cloth shops; in villages salt-making, cutting toddy palms and raiding salt depots; Eluru National School volunteers joined in May 1930.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT written by Gandhi?
q.x: The Discovery of India is Nehru's; the other three are Gandhi's.

q.s: The Rs 2 per kg rice scheme in Andhra Pradesh was introduced in 1983 by:
q.x: NTR introduced Rs 2 a kg rice along with subsidised housing and Janata cloth.

q.s: The States Reorganisation Commission (1955) was headed by:
q.x: Fazl Ali chaired it; Panikkar and Kunzru were members; S.K. Dar headed the 1948 commission.

q.s: The States Reorganisation Commission recommended a separate state for:
q.x: It proposed Vidarbha as a separate state and rejected the Punjabi Suba demand.

q.s: The Eight-Point Formula on Telangana was announced in April 1969 by:
q.x: Indira Gandhi announced it on 11 April 1969 during the Jai Telangana agitation.

q.s: After bifurcation in 2014, Telangana's Legislative Assembly has how many seats?
q.x: Telangana has 119 Assembly seats; residuary Andhra Pradesh has 175.

q.s: How many Lok Sabha seats were allotted to Andhra Pradesh after bifurcation?
q.x: AP has 25 Lok Sabha seats and Telangana 17 (together the old 42).

q.s: The Ikshvaku capital Vijayapuri was situated at:
q.x: Vijayapuri is at Nagarjunakonda in the Krishna valley.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT an Ikshvaku ruler?
q.x: Gautamiputra Satakarni was a Satavahana king.

q.s: Hala's Gathasaptasati is an anthology of 700 verses in:
q.x: The Gathasaptasati is in Maharashtri Prakrit and preserves early Telugu words.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT written by Srinatha?
q.x: Andhra Mahabhagavatamu is Bammera Pothana's work.

q.s: The greatest of the Parthian (Pahlava) kings in India was:
q.x: Gondophares is known from the Takht-i-Bahi inscription; tradition brings St Thomas to his court.

q.s: According to Christian tradition, St Thomas came to the court of:
q.x: Tradition links St Thomas with the Parthian king Gondophares.

q.s: On the basis of the Myakadoni inscription, V.S. Sukthankar placed the original home of the Satavahanas in the:
q.x: Sukthankar cited the Myakadoni record for Bellary; Rapson favoured the eastern Deccan (Andhra).

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: R.G. Bhandarkar held that the Andhras and the Satavahanas were different.
E.J. Rapson placed the origin of the Satavahanas in the eastern Deccan.
Nilakanta Sastri took 'Satavahana' as a tribal name.
Sukthankar placed the Satavahana home in Vidarbha.
q.x: Rapson favoured Andhra; Bhandarkar held them the same; Sastri took 'Andhra' as tribal; Sukthankar chose Bellary.

q.s: The Prajnaparamita Shastra is attributed to:
q.x: Nagarjuna's Mahayana work; Kundakunda wrote Samayasara, Kutuhala Lilavati Parinayam.

q.s: Samayasara, an important Jain text, was written by:
q.x: Kundakundacharya wrote the Samayasara.

q.s: Which classical writer complained of the drain of Roman money to India for luxuries?
q.x: Pliny put the drain at about 12.5 million denarii a year, spent on spices, gems and fine textiles.

q.s: The Naneghat inscription of Devi Naganika records the sacrifices performed by:
q.x: It records two Ashvamedhas and a Rajasuya by Satakarni I.

q.s: Which of the following was a port on the Andhra coast in the Ikshvaku period?
q.x: Ghantasala (Kantakasala) and Motupalli were Andhra ports; the others lay outside Andhra.

q.s: Which Ikshvaku king gave gold, cows, ploughs and agraharas to Brahmins and performed Vedic sacrifices?
q.x: Vasishthiputra Sri Santamula (Chamtamula) was the Vedic sacrificer and donor.

q.s: The Kondamudi copper plates, found near Tenali, were issued by the Brihatphalayana king:
q.x: Jayavarma issued them in his 10th year from Kuduru, granting Panthur to eight Brahmins.

q.s: Ganitasarasangraha, a Sanskrit work on mathematics, was written in the Rashtrakuta court by:
q.x: Mahaviracharya wrote it under Amoghavarsha I.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a Rashtrakuta ruler?
q.x: Pulakeshin II was a Chalukya of Badami.

q.s: Pampa, author of the Vikramarjuna Vijaya (a Mahabharata), wrote in:
q.x: Pampa wrote in Kannada; Sarala Dasa's Mahabharata is in Odia, Kasirama Das's in Bengali.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of Mahabharata composer and language is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Sarala Dasa wrote in Odia.

q.s: Kreedabhiramam, a Telugu vidhi natakam set in Warangal, is attributed to:
q.x: Vinukonda Vallabharaya rendered Ravipati Tripurantakudu's Premabhiramam.

q.s: The Kakatiya rulers belonged to which varna?
q.x: The Kakatiyas were Shudras by varna.

q.s: In Kakatiya village society the Ayagars were:
o: Military chiefs under the nayankara system
q.x: Ayagars were village servants remunerated with land free of cess or tax.

q.s: Which Vijayanagara ruler bore the title 'Gajabetekara' (hunter of elephants)?
q.x: Deva Raya II also enlisted Muslim archers, according to Ferishta.

q.s: Deva Raya II expelled the Gajapati Veerabhanu Deva and restored as his feudatories the Reddis of:
q.x: He restored the Rajahmundry Reddis in 1429.

q.s: By the Inqiyad Nama (1636), Mughal suzerainty was accepted by the Golconda ruler:
q.x: Abdullah Qutb Shah (r. 1626-72) accepted Shah Jahan's suzerainty.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the five Deccan Sultanates?
q.x: The five were Bijapur, Golconda, Ahmednagar, Berar and Bidar.

q.s: The first Vijayanagara-Bahmani war was fought in the reign of:
q.x: Bukka I fought Muhammad Shah I (1362-67).

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a ruler of the Sangama dynasty?
q.x: Krishnadevaraya belonged to the Tuluva dynasty.

q.s: Krishnadevaraya assumed the title 'Yavana Rajya Sthapanacharya' after restoring to the throne:
q.x: After the Raichur-Bidar campaign he freed Mahmud Shah from Barid and restored him; Manucharitra celebrates it.

q.s: Who was the Prime Minister (Appaji) of Krishnadevaraya?
q.x: Saluva Timmarusu was later blinded on suspicion; Vyasatirtha was the rajaguru.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the Ashtadiggajas of Krishnadevaraya's court?
q.x: Srinatha belonged to the Reddi period, a century earlier.

q.s: Krishnadevaraya's court hall of poets was called:
q.x: Bhuvana Vijayam ('conquest of the world') housed the Ashtadiggajas; Kavula Samstha is what the Tippalur record calls the poets.

q.s: The Tippalur agrahara in Kadapa was gifted to the court poets by:
q.x: Krishnadevaraya, not Achyutaraya, gave the Tippalur agrahara.

q.s: In Vijayanagara central administration, the Bhandara department looked after the:

q.s: Under the Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017, a creche is mandatory in establishments with:

POCSO was merged into the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

POCSO was drafted by the Ministry of Home Affairs.

q.s: The Jai Andhra agitation (1972-73) was brought to an end by the:

q.x: Karmayogi (2020) moves training from rule-based to role-based capacity building.

q.s: YSR Cheyutha in Andhra Pradesh was meant for BC, SC, ST and minority women in the age group of:

India joined the IMF only after the 1991 crisis.

Non-use of force except in self-defence and defence of the mandate

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a federal feature of the Indian Constitution?

No State has the right to secede from the Indian Union.
